idea.value: A 31.5 s silent product film for an AI assistant inside a business web portal: a kinetic-type premise on two grounds names what it is and whom it serves, then two real prompts are typed and answered on screen, and a three-line benefit list and a short tagline close it. The proof is the interface answering, not a claim.

audience.value: Professional intermediaries who answer client questions about plans and coverage (the type addresses them directly as the audience at 3.4-5.6 s, and the prompts ask for plan comparisons and coverage of one item). Inferred from the on-screen copy; no voice.

value.device: giant word pulled back to reading size, then a soft light sweeps off the product name
value.description: F0 opens on a short greeting word so large it overflows both frame edges (at least 73% of frame width visible, about 2.5x its settled size); it pulls back on an expo.out ease and settles by F14 (0.58 s) at 43% of frame width, centred. A hard cut at F17 (0.708 s) puts the product name on the same white ground, half hidden under a soft blue light that slides right and off it in 9 frames (F17-F26). The viewer is introduced before being told anything, and the name is uncovered rather than shown.

evidence: motion.json s001 camera.ease expo.out, t5Sec 0.068 to t95Sec 0.496

value.purpose: Introduce: greeting word, then the product name
value.retentionDevice: scale pull-back and a light that uncovers the name
value.content: Two-word greeting and product name, dark navy and brand blue on a near-white ground with a soft blue light at the edge

value.purpose: Define: what it is and whom it is for, one phrase at a time
value.retentionDevice: ground swap to saturated blue, words added one by one, type size stepping down each phrase
value.content: Category phrase in white on saturated blue (two swaps), then the audience and the place it lives in navy on white, each line smaller than the last

value.purpose: Demonstrate 1: a comparison question typed and answered with a table

value.content: Assistant start screen; prompt typed in close-up; send button macro; chat with a working indicator; a two-column comparison table resolves

value.purpose: Reset the energy and list the three benefits

value.content: Prompt field on a sky-blue gradient, the call-to-ask line typed, a click, then a card with three benefit rows whose check circles fill in turn

value.purpose: Demonstrate 2: a yes/no coverage question answered in plain language
value.retentionDevice: large typed question with the camera following the caret, then a streamed answer
value.content: Question typed at headline size, the chat shows a working indicator, then a short affirmative answer streams in line by line

value.purpose: Name the pain removed, then the product and its promise
value.retentionDevice: fade to a ground with a blue corner glow; words fade up one by one; wordmark revealed left to right with a two-part tagline
value.content: One negative-benefit sentence, then the lower-case wordmark with a two-clause tagline beneath

value.purpose: Call to action and where to find it
value.retentionDevice: two hard text swaps on a held ground
value.content: Imperative two-word line, then one line naming where the assistant is built in

payoff.value: The comparison table at 14.2-15.3 s: after a question too long to read, a full two-plan table resolves in under a second, and the music drops out for 0.7 s while it sits on screen. The second, shorter answer (21.7-25.6 s) repeats the proof in plain language.

callToAction.value: A two-word imperative using the product name (29.58-30.50 s), then one line saying it is built into the portal the audience already uses (30.50-31.54 s). No URL, no button, no logo lock-up beyond the earlier wordmark.

whyItWorks: The premise is one sentence split across six lines and three grounds (1.6-5.6 s), so it reads as motion rather than a paragraph; each line is 10-30% smaller than the last, which lands the type at the interface's own text size when the UI dissolves in at 5.6 s.
The demo is real interface at reading scale: the camera cuts in (about 1.8x) while the prompt is typed and back out once it overflows, so the viewer reads the question without a zoom animation.
Waits are shown but compressed: the working indicator holds 2.5 s and the answer resolves through a shimmer placeholder in 0.9 s, so the speed of the answer is the claim.

The second half is louder (section energy 0.14 -> 0.48) and holds a little longer (median hold 1.17 s before 15.29 s, 1.46 s after, the two answers being the longest); the near-silence just before 15.29 s marks the turn.
Outgoing shots end on an accelerating drift and incoming shots continue it, so hard cuts on a white ground feel like one camera.
